draft.title: Adding and scaling vectors
card: To add vectors, add the matching components. If a = 3i + 2j and b = i − 4j, then a + b = 4i − 2j. Drawn as arrows, you place the tail of b at the head of a (head to tail).
To subtract, subtract the matching components. a − b = (3 − 1)i + (2 − (−4))j = 2i + 6j. Take care with the sign when the second component is negative.
A scalar is an ordinary number. Multiplying a vector by a scalar k multiplies every component by k. So 2a = 6i + 4j.
If k > 1, the vector gets longer. If 0 < k < 1, it gets shorter. If k is negative, the vector points the opposite way. So −a = −3i − 2j.
draft.remember: Add or scale each component. A negative scalar reverses the direction.

a.q: Let p = 2i + 5j and q = 4i − j. What is p + q?
a.why: Add the i components: 2 + 4 = 6. Add the j components: 5 + (−1) = 4. So p + q = 6i + 4j. The option 6i + 6j comes from ignoring the negative sign on the j component of q.
a.clue: Add the i parts together and the j parts together.

b.q: Let u = 3i − 2j and v = i + 4j. What is 2u − v?
b.why: 2u = 6i − 4j. Subtract v: (6 − 1)i + (−4 − 4)j = 5i − 8j. The option 5i + 2j comes from the sign error of adding 4 to −4... no: it comes from treating −4 − 4 as −4 + 4 + 2, while the correct step is subtracting 4 from −4.
b.clue: Scale u first, then subtract each component of v.

problems.detail: The why for (b) contains leftover drafting text ('... no:'). Its account of the 5i + 2j distractor ('treating −4 − 4 as −4 + 4 + 2') is nonsensical. That option actually comes from not scaling the j component of u and adding instead of subtracting: −2 + 4 = 2. Rewrite it so students see the real error.

check.summary: Both questions have one correct answer (6i + 4j and 5i − 8j), and the card is accurate. The explanation for (b) is garbled, with leftover drafting text and a wrong account of how the 5i + 2j distractor arises, so it needs rewriting.

final.title: Adding and scaling vectors
card: To add vectors, add the matching components. If \(a = 3i + 2j\) and \(b = i - 4j\), then \(a + b = 4i - 2j\). Drawn as arrows, you place the tail of \(b\) at the head of a (head to tail).
To subtract, subtract the matching components. \(a - b = (3 - 1)i + (2 - (-4))j = 2i + 6j\). Take care with the sign when the second component is negative.
A scalar is an ordinary number. Multiplying a vector by a scalar \(k\) multiplies every component by \(k\). So \(2a = 6i + 4j\).
If \(k > 1\), the vector gets longer. If \(0 < k < 1\), it gets shorter. If \(k\) is negative, the vector points the opposite way. So \(-a = -3i - 2j\).
final.remember: Add or scale each component. A negative scalar reverses the direction.

a.q: Let \(p = 2i + 5j\) and \(q = 4i - j\). What is \(p + q\)?
a.why: Add the \(i\) components: \(2 + 4 = 6\). Add the \(j\) components: \(5 + (-1) = 4\). So \(p + q = 6i + 4j\). The option \(6i + 6j\) comes from ignoring the negative sign on the \(j\) component of \(q\).
a.clue: Add the \(i\) parts together and the \(j\) parts together.

b.q: Let \(u = 3i - 2j\) and \(v = i + 4j\). What is \(2u - v\)?
b.why: First \(2u = 6i - 4j\). Then \(2u - v = (6 - 1)i + (-4 - 4)j = 5i - 8j\). The option \(5i + 2j\) comes from two slips: leaving the \(j\) part of \(u\) as \(-2\) instead of doubling it, then adding 4 instead of subtracting it, so \(-2 + 4 = 2\).
b.clue: Scale \(u\) first, then subtract each component of \(v\).
